title: Degeneracy-reshaped spin squeezing in high-spin Fermi-Hubbard systems weakly coupled to light
abstract: We study spin squeezing in strongly interacting high-spin Fermi-Hubbard systems weakly coupled to light. We show that spin squeezing dynamics is qualitatively modified by the degeneracies associated with the internal spin structure. We identify these degeneracies as the microscopic origin of the breakdown of conventional maximal-spin description and develop an effective framework based on population eigenstates that quantitatively reproduces spin squeezing evolution. Our results uncover a generic mechanism by which degeneracy reshapes collective spin dynamics.
summary: The paper analyzes spin squeezing in high-spin Fermi-Hubbard systems coupled to light, finding that simple models fail due to internal degeneracies. The authors develop an effective framework using Population Eigenstates (PES) to accurately capture the modified collective spin dynamics caused by these uncaptured degenerate states.
main_problem: The study investigates how spin squeezing dynamics are modified by internal degeneracies when analyzing high-spin Fermi-Hubbard systems weakly coupled to light.
main_result: Degeneracy associated with the internal spin structure causes conventional maximal-spin descriptions (like those based on Dicke states) to break down, necessitating an effective framework built upon Population Eigenstates (PES).
method: The authors employ perturbative techniques, including Schrieffer-Wolff transformations, to derive effective Hamiltonians by projecting the full Hamiltonian onto various degenerate manifolds.
model_or_system: The system is a Fermi-Hubbard model realized with high-spin fermionic atoms in an optical lattice. The dynamics are governed by tunneling ($J$), on-site repulsion ($U$), and weak coupling to light ($\hat{V}_{soc}$).
key_observables: Spin squeezing parameter ($\xi^2$) and total spin dynamics ($\langle\hat{\mathbf{J}}^2angle$).
important_parameters: High nuclear spin $s \ge 1$, strongly repulsive regime ($U \gg J$), and weak light coupling ($\Omega_{soc}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on perturbative expansions (e.g., Schrieffer-Wolff up to second order) and the identification of different energy manifolds (Dicke, GPES, $q$-PES).
figures_summary: Figures compare spin squeezing ($\xi^2$) and total spin dynamics for various approximations (full model vs. Dicke projection vs. GPES projection) across different high-spin regimes ($s=1, s=3/2$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the predictions of simple models (like OAT or Dicke projections) against the full dynamics derived from incorporating higher-order degenerate states captured by the Population Eigenstates basis.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it addresses the limitations of standard collective spin approximations in complex, high-spin quantum systems, providing a necessary theoretical refinement for modeling light-matter interactions in ultracold atomic gases.

Examples of the four dynamical descriptions considered in this work, ˆHFH+ ˆVsoc, ˆHSE+ ˆVsoc, ˆH(soc) GPES, and ˆH(soc) Dicke, shown on a common timescale determined by χ = 1/12 000, for different values of (U, Ωsoc). The dynamics generated by ˆHFH + ˆVsoc (solid red line) serve as the most accurate reference. The spin-exchange description ˆHSE + ˆVsoc remains quantitatively accurate for J/U ≲2.0, while the effective GPES Hamiltonian ˆH(soc) GPES reproduces ˆHSE + ˆVsoc dynamics for Ωsoc/Eq ≲0.05. Within the range of system sizes and atomic spins investigated, the bounds J/U ≲2.0 and Ωsoc/Eq ≲0.05 appear to be universal.
